authority: diagnostic: paper only, not investment advice
flags: Danaos announced in a 6-K that it is exploring a carve-out and sale of a minority stake in its dry bulk segment, with a possible equity placement and listing in the Norwegian market. It has mandated investment banks, and the filing says no transaction is assured.

Danaos entered into additional JOLCO financing arrangements for six operating container vessels. They are accounted for as failed sale-leasebacks and financing arrangements, so the vessels stay on the balance sheet and the proceeds are recorded as financing liabilities.

Certain container vessels' time charters were ended early under termination agreements. This produced a $5.1 million gain recorded in voyage expenses, because bunkers were retained on redelivery at no consideration.
no_value_reason: some filed figures are years older than the latest annual report

business_model.claim: Danaos owns ships and earns charter hire. It charters container vessels to large liner companies and employs drybulk (Capesize) vessels on short-term time charters and voyage charters.
quotes: Danaos Corporation is an international owner of container vessels and drybulk vessels, chartering our container vessels to many of the world’s largest liner companies and employing our drybulk vessels on short-term time charters and voyage charters.

business_model.claim: Customers are mainly major container liner companies, including CMA CGM, MSC, Hapag Lloyd, COSCO, Maersk, ONE, OOCL, Yang Ming and ZIM.
quotes: As of February 25, 2026, these customers included CMA CGM, MSC, Hapag Lloyd, COSCO, PIL, Maersk, ONE, Sealead, OOCL, Samudera, Interasia Lines, Yang Ming and ZIM.

business_model.claim: The asset base is a fleet of 75 owned containerships (477,491 TEUs), 27 containerships under construction (174,550 TEUs) and 11 Capesize bulk carriers, counting one due for delivery.
quotes: we owned 75 containerships aggregating 477,491 TEUs, 27 under construction containerships aggregating 174,550 TEUs, 11 Capesize bulk carriers

business_model.basis: stated in the cited items; the segment net income measure comes from the interim 6-K
business_model.claim: The company reports two segments: container vessels (time and bareboat charters) and drybulk vessels (time and voyage charters). The chief executive, as chief operating decision maker, judges each segment on its net income and uses it to allocate capital between them.
quotes: the Company operates in two separate segments in accordance with ASC 280: (i) a container vessels segment, as a provider of worldwide marine transportation services through time charter and bareboat charter arrangements; and (ii) a drybulk vessels segment, as a provider of drybulk commodity transportation services through time charter and voyage charter arrangements.

business_model.claim: Annual operating revenues were 1,042,456 (table in thousands of USD) against 1,014,110 a year earlier. Net income was 494,614 against 505,073 (table in thousands). Revenue rose while net income fell.
The company names fleet size as the primary driver of revenue. Charter rates are the other principal driver, alongside utilization.
quotes: The number of vessels in our fleet, and their TEU capacity for containerships or DWT capacity for drybulk vessels, is the primary factor in determining the level of our revenues.

business_model.claim: Multi-year fixed-rate charters give contracted revenue visibility: total contracted cash operating revenues of $4.3 billion, including newbuildings, and a remaining average contracted containership charter duration of 4.3 years.
quotes: Total contracted cash operating revenues, based on concluded charter contracts through the date of this annual report, currently stand at $4.3 billion, including newbuildings.

business_model.claim: Contracted future minimum charter payments for the operating and chartered newbuilding container vessels total $4,153.4 (table in millions of USD). Four newbuilding containerships without time charters are excluded.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited item; the mechanism is inferred from the revenue driver discussion
business_model.claim: Container vessel utilization was 98.2% in the latest fiscal year versus 97.2% the year before. Utilization matters because hire accrues over operating days and off-hire time cuts revenue.
quotes: During 2025, our container vessels fleet utilization was 98.2%, compared to 97.2% in 2024, and 97.7% in 2023.

business_model.claim: The drybulk segment is a spot-market business with revenue that moves with Capesize rates. Its time charter equivalent rate was $30,401 per day in the second quarter versus $17,934 a year earlier, and segment revenue was $35.7 million versus $22.7 million.
quotes: The increase was primarily driven by a significant improvement in Time Charter Equivalent rate per day, which increased to $30,401 per day in the three months ended June 30, 2026, from $17,934 per day in the three months ended June 30, 2025, reflecting improved market conditions, as well as the operation of an additional vessel in our drybulk fleet.

business_model.claim: Container segment revenue is large and roughly flat, while drybulk is smaller and growing. In the second quarter, container revenue was $238.6 million versus $239.4 million, and total operating revenues were $274.4 million versus $262.2 million.

Costs vary with charter type. Under voyage and time charters Danaos pays vessel operating expenses. Under bareboat charters the charterer bears substantially all of them. Under multi-year time and bareboat charters charterers bear most voyage expenses, while voyage charters leave voyage costs with Danaos.
quotes: Under voyage charters and time charters, we pay for vessel operating expenses.

business_model.basis: stated in the income statement; the mechanism is stated in the operating review
business_model.claim: The main annual cost lines were vessel operating expenses of (208,779), depreciation of (163,366), general and administrative expenses of (64,410) and amortization of drydocking and special survey costs of (44,074) (table in thousands, shown as expenses).

Management services come from related parties. The Manager and Danaos Chartering are ultimately owned by DIL, the largest stockholder, so part of the cost base is fees paid to affiliates, including a 1.25% brokerage fee that stays at that rate in 2026.
quotes: Our Manager and Danaos Chartering are ultimately owned by DIL, which is also our largest stockholder.

business_model.basis: stated in the statements; the link between borrowing and interest cost is inferred
business_model.claim: Fleet growth is financed with operating cash flow and debt, which adds interest cost. Operating cash flow was 644,753 and proceeds from long-term debt were 620,675. Interest expense and finance costs rose to (42,842) from (26,185) (tables in thousands).

In October the company said it is exploring a carve-out and sale of a minority stake in its dry bulk segment, with a possible equity placement and listing in Norway. The announcement says no transaction is assured.
quotes: exploring a carve-out and sale of a minority stake in its dry bulk segment
There can be no assurance that any transaction or listing will be pursued or completed, or as to its terms or timing.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in P1. The 'one of the largest' ranking is the company's own description and no peer data is in the evidence.
competitive_position.claim: Danaos describes itself as one of the largest containership operating lessors. At the fleet date in the 20-F it owned 75 containerships totalling 477,491 TEUs, with 27 more containerships of 174,550 TEUs under construction.
quotes: Danaos is one of the largest containership operating lessors in the world.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in P1. The 20-F's own minimum-payments table (P2) is a separate, slightly different measure.
competitive_position.claim: Multi-year charters give contracted revenue visibility. Contracted cash operating revenues from concluded charters, including newbuildings, stand at $4.3 billion. The remaining average containership charter duration is 4.3 years, and initial charter terms run up to 18 years.
quotes: Total contracted cash operating revenues, based on concluded charter contracts through the date of this annual report, currently stand at $4.3 billion, including newbuildings.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in P1 and P2. No per-customer revenue concentration is given in the packet.
competitive_position.claim: The customer base is diversified across major liner companies. Named charterers include CMA CGM, MSC, Hapag Lloyd, COSCO, Maersk, ONE, OOCL, Yang Ming and ZIM.
quotes: Our strategy is to charter our containerships under multi-year, fixed-rate period charters to a diverse group of liner companies, including many of the largest companies globally, as measured by TEU capacity.

competitive_position.claim: Container fleet utilization is high. It was 98.2% in the 20-F year against 97.2% the year before. In the second quarter of 2026 it was 97.7% against 98.4% a year earlier.
quotes: During 2025, our container vessels fleet utilization was 98.2%, compared to 97.2% in 2024, and 97.7% in 2023.

competitive_position.basis: Table and text stated in P2.
competitive_position.claim: Contracted coverage of operating days falls steeply with distance. It is 99.5% in the nearest period, 72.6% in the next, 37.2% in the third and 9.6% in the furthest. Fleet earnings therefore depend on re-chartering at future market rates.
quotes: to the extent charter rates are at levels lower than were prevailing when we entered into expiring charters, we may have to re-charter these vessels for rates lower than the level of their current charter rates.

competitive_position.claim: Near-term roll-over is limited. As of the fleet date, two containerships' charters expire in the first following year and 21 in the second.
quotes: As of February 25, 2026, the charters for two of our containerships are scheduled to expire in 2026 and 21 in 2027.

competitive_position.claim: The newbuilding programme renews and expands the fleet. Since the start of 2022 Danaos ordered 35 newbuilding containerships of 232,948 TEU for $2.7 billion, eight of them delivered. Time charters averaging approximately 5.8 years are contracted for 21 of the 27 vessels under construction.
quotes: Since the beginning of 2022, we have ordered 35 newbuilding containerships with an aggregate capacity of 232,948 TEU, eight of which have been delivered to us, for an aggregate purchase price of $2.7 billion.

competitive_position.claim: Part of the orderbook is not yet chartered. Four newbuilding containerships had no charter arrangements in place at the end of the 20-F year, and the contracted minimum-payments table excludes them.
quotes: four newbuilding container vessels for which no charter arrangements are currently in place

competitive_position.basis: Fleet age is stated in P1. Its competitive effect is inferred from the company's own description of the newbuildings.
competitive_position.claim: The fleet is middle-aged but being renewed. The containership fleet's average age weighted by TEU is about 15.2 years, excluding newbuildings. The orderbook is described as eco-designed to the latest IMO standards.
quotes: All vessels in our orderbook are designed with the latest eco characteristics

competitive_position.basis: Figures stated in F2. The cause is inferred from the statement of income and P2, which says aggregate expenses increase as the fleet grows.
competitive_position.claim: Financial capacity supports the position, but profitability is under cost pressure. Operating revenues rose to 1,042,456 from 1,014,110 (table in thousands of USD), while operating income fell to 498,766 from 540,884. Vessel operating expenses rose to 208,779 from 185,724, and depreciation rose to 163,366 from 148,344.

competitive_position.basis: Figures stated in F1, F2 and F3. The link to newbuilding funding is inferred.
competitive_position.claim: Liquidity strengthened but debt is rising to fund growth. Cash was 1,037,292 against 453,384 (table in thousands of USD), and operating cash flow was 644,753. Long-term debt, net, rose to 872,076 from 699,563, and the current portion rose to 283,015 from 35,220. Interest expense and finance costs rose to 42,842 from 26,185.

The dry bulk segment adds diversification but also spot-market exposure. The segment comprises 11 Capesize vessels, plus four Newcastlemax bulk carriers ordered for $297.3 million. Danaos states that it is exposed to spot market rates.
quotes: We currently intend to charter our drybulk vessels primarily on short-term time charters and voyage charters, and we are therefore exposed to fluctuations in the corresponding spot market rates.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in P4. The container-segment reading, that growth is not rate-led, is inferred from the listed drivers.
competitive_position.claim: In the second quarter of 2026 drybulk revenue rose 57.3% to $35.7 million from $22.7 million, with the TCE rate at $30,401 per day against $17,934. In the same quarter container-segment revenue was slightly lower at $238.6 million against $239.4 million, and higher charter rates added only $0.6 million.
quotes: reflecting improved market conditions, as well as the operation of an additional vessel in our drybulk fleet.

competitive_position.claim: Danaos depends on the willingness and ability of its charterers to pay, and the company says a charterer failure would materially hurt results.
quotes: If the charterers are unable or unwilling to make charter payments to us, our results of operations and financial condition will be materially adversely affected.

competitive_position.basis: Stated in P1 and P2. The competitive implication is inferred.

financial_health.claim: Leverage is moderate relative to equity. Total liabilities were 1,318,353 against total stockholders' equity of 3,795,577 and total assets of 5,113,930 (table in thousands). Long-term debt, net was 872,076 plus a current portion of 283,015.

The company generates substantial operating cash. Net cash provided by operating activities was 644,753 (table in thousands), up from 621,750 and 576,292 in the two prior years, and above net income of 494,614.

financial_health.basis: Revenue and income figures are stated in F2; the quote is from P1 (the 18-year charter term is also in P1); utilization is stated in P2. The quality assessment is inferred.
financial_health.claim: Cash quality is supported by recurring charter revenue and by the absence of income tax. Operating revenues were 1,042,456 and operating income was 498,766 (table in thousands). Income taxes were 0.
quotes: Our charters have initial terms ranging up to 18 years, which provide us with stable cash flows and high utilization rates.

financial_health.claim: Cash was used heavily for fleet investment and shareholder returns. Vessel additions and advances were (296,690), dividends paid were (63,550) and stock repurchases were (75,739) (table in thousands). Net cash used in investing was (325,696).

Cash rose partly through new borrowing. Proceeds from long-term debt were 620,675 against payments and prepayments of (190,764) (table in thousands), and net financing cash flow was 264,851. Interest expense and finance costs rose to (42,842) from (26,185).

financial_health.basis: Debt figures are stated in F1; the repayment route is inferred from F1 and F3.

Contracted charter income supports debt service. Future minimum charter payments were $4,153.4 (table in millions), of which $945.8 (table in millions) fall in the first year. Contracted cash operating revenues are stated as $4.3 billion including newbuildings.

growth_thesis.basis: Order and delivery figures are stated in the 20-F; the mechanism is stated in Item 5 and partly inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Containership newbuildings are the main fleet-growth pipeline: 35 ships of 232,948 TEU have been ordered since the start of 2022 for $2.7 billion, and 27 containerships of 174,550 TEUs are still under construction. For this to keep driving growth, the yards must deliver on schedule and the ships must start earning on their charters.
quotes: Since the beginning of 2022, we have ordered 35 newbuilding containerships with an aggregate capacity of 232,948 TEU, eight of which have been delivered to us, for an aggregate purchase price of $2.7 billion.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the cited 20-F text; the share of days contracted is read from the Item 5 table.
growth_thesis.claim: A multi-year charter backlog gives revenue visibility: total contracted cash operating revenues are $4.3 billion, the remaining average contracted charter duration is 4.3 years, and containership utilization was 98.2% in 2025. Growth from this driver requires charterers to keep honouring contracts and expiring charters to be re-let at acceptable rates.
quotes: Total contracted cash operating revenues, based on concluded charter contracts through the date of this annual report, currently stand at $4.3 billion, including newbuildings.

growth_thesis.basis: Revenue and TCE figures are stated in the 6-K; the dependence on market rates is stated in the 20-F Item 5.
growth_thesis.claim: The drybulk segment is the fastest-growing revenue line in 2026: first-half drybulk revenue rose to $59.9 million from $39.8 million, and TCE rate per day rose to $28,007 from $14,386. For this to continue, Capesize market rates must stay firm and utilization must hold.
quotes: Operating revenues of our drybulk vessels segment increased by 50.5%, or $20.1 million, to $59.9 million in the six months ended June 30, 2026, compared to $39.8 million of revenues in the six months ended June 30, 2025.

growth_thesis.basis: Vessel counts and price are stated in the 20-F; the funding role of the carve-out is inferred from the 6-K.
growth_thesis.claim: The drybulk fleet is being extended: 11 Capesize vessels are on a fully delivered basis, and four Newcastlemax bulk carriers ordered in early 2026 cost $297.3 million in aggregate. The company is also exploring a minority-stake carve-out and listing of the dry bulk business. Whether this adds growth depends on the Newcastlemaxes being delivered and on a transaction being pursued, which is not assured.
quotes: There can be no assurance that any transaction or listing will be pursued or completed, or as to its terms or timing.

growth_thesis.basis: Figures come from the statements; the link between financing and the newbuild programme is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: The expansion is being financed from strong operating cash flow plus new debt. Cash rose to 1,037,292 from 453,384 (table in thousands), operating cash flow was 644,753, and long-term debt proceeds were 620,675, against vessel additions and advances of 296,690. Growth requires continued cash generation and access to debt.

growth_thesis.basis: Inferred from the income statement and cash flow statement.
growth_thesis.claim: Per-share growth is supported by buybacks: diluted EPS was $26.76 against $26.05, even though net income fell to 494,614 from 505,073 (table in thousands). Weighted average basic shares fell to 18,432,153 from 19,316,453, and 75,739 was spent repurchasing stock. This continues only if repurchases continue while the company funds its fleet programme.

growth_thesis.basis: Inferred from the income statement; the link between fleet size and expenses is stated in Item 5.
growth_thesis.claim: Revenue growth has so far been modest and has not lifted operating profit: revenues rose to 1,042,456 from 1,014,110, while operating income fell to 498,766 from 540,884 (table in thousands). New capacity therefore has to earn enough to cover higher vessel operating, depreciation and G&A costs before it adds to profit growth.
